title: Peter Chan Brought a Chengdu Dementia Care Home's Motto to Toronto
excerpt: The veteran filmmaker drew on guidance from a Chengdu Alzheimer's care facility — "go with the flow, know when to stop" — while directing his early-onset dementia drama, starring Zhou Xun, which premieres at TIFF on September 18.
body:
• Peter Chan says eight words from a Chengdu Alzheimer's care home — shun shi er wei, shi ke er zhi ("go with the flow, know when to stop") — shaped nearly every directing decision on The Road Not Taken.
  • The facility is known for keeping patients from deteriorating rapidly. Its counsel to families: don't correct them, don't argue, follow wherever their reality has drifted — but know when to let go.
  • The 135-minute Mandarin drama stars Zhou Xun as a celebrated television host confronting early-onset Alzheimer's, and has its world premiere in TIFF's Special Presentations on September 18, 2026.
  • Chan rewrote a script that had been in development since the COVID-19 pandemic from scratch, keeping a single line, determined not to make "an issue movie about a disease."

Peter Chan Ho-sun did not find the directing philosophy of The Road Not Taken on a film set. He found it in a dementia care home in Chengdu. While researching his latest feature — an early-onset Alzheimer's drama starring Zhou Xun that premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 18 — Chan visited what he calls one of the finest Alzheimer's care facilities in the city, one known for managing patients without their condition rapidly worsening. He left with eight words that governed nearly every choice he made on the film: shun shi er wei, shi ke er zhi — go with the flow, know when to stop.

A motto with two lives

The phrase was not meant for filmmakers. It was the facility's guidance for families of dementia patients — don't correct them, don't argue — but Chan applied the same rule to himself as a director.

"Go with the flow, know when to stop, because that's how an Alzheimer patient's family should treat an Alzheimer patient. Not just for Alzheimer patients, but also for a director."

— Peter Chan, in an interview with Variety

Chan told Variety he was determined not to turn the material into an issue movie about a disease. The motto gave him the discipline for that refusal: a directive not to wrestle the story of decline into a tidy shape.

A script years in the making

The Road Not Taken did not start as Chan's to direct. The script arrived as a completed draft that had been in development since the COVID-19 pandemic, before he made She's Got No Name. Chan read it, liked it, and stepped back — he intended only to produce while another director took over. Several filmmakers cycled through the project. Once She's Got No Name wrapped, the producers and an already-cast ensemble came back to him. Chan rewrote the script from scratch, keeping a single line from the original draft, and worked through it with an assistant — his written Chinese, he says, trails his spoken fluency because his formal Chinese schooling ended in the sixth grade.

The China-Hong Kong co-production, from We Pictures Limited and ChengDu J.Q. Pictures, stars Zhou Xun alongside Tian Zhuangzhuang, Diana Lin, Vicky Chen, and Zhang Youhao. Chan, born in Hong Kong in 1962 and best known for Comrades, Almost a Love Story and the Zhang Ziyi-starring She's Got No Name, studied film at UCLA before returning to Hong Kong in 1983.

What it says about caregiving

The Chengdu facility's advice sits within person-centered dementia care, which treats confusion as something to meet rather than misbehavior to correct. What makes Chan's borrowing striking is how little adaptation it needed: the same eight words counsel a daughter in Chengdu and a director on set.

The "know when to stop" half reads, in this context, as a rebuke to the genre's usual temptations — sentimentality on one side, didacticism on the other. Dementia resists the recovery arcs films crave; Chan's film refuses to impose one.

"Shun shi er wei, shi ke er zhi — go with the flow, know when to stop."

— The eight words from the Chengdu dementia care home that shaped the film

An uneasy question for diaspora families

Across the South Asian diaspora, dementia is still often handled behind closed doors — absorbed by families, sometimes undiagnosed, with correction as the default response to confusion. A care home in Chengdu counseling families to stop arguing with a drifting mind, and to recognize when letting go is the kinder act, names a tension many diaspora caregivers of aging immigrant parents know well: the pull between filial duty that says keep fighting and the acceptance that says yield.

What's next

The Road Not Taken has its world premiere on September 18, 2026, in the Special Presentations section of the Toronto International Film Festival. No wider release date has been announced. Distribution is handled by Moebius Entertainment Limited and We Distribution Limited.
